feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is stated for it. Evidence: iteration 7 (mass 0.6 kg, body_length 0.12 m, wheel_track 0.10 m) scored 707.2, the best so far. Its s-bend finished 20/20 with steering_oscillation 0.311, and its oval finished 20/20 at 1.79 s. Its slalom stayed at 0/20, but mean progress rose from 0.30 to 0.53 and line_loss_events rose to 1.3, with max_error 0.0653. Iteration 4 versus iteration 1 (wheel_track 0.12 to 0.10 m) gave a small slalom gain with the oval unchanged, which suggests turn authority is the lever. Lowering wheel_track further is the next step. The Integrator's controller gains are kept fixed so the change isolates the track. Next-race rules: if slalom line_loss_events fall to about 1.0 or below and s-bend steering_oscillation stays under 0.35, keep wheel_track 0.09 m and look at whether the slalom gets its first finishes. If line loss rises again with max_error still near 0.065, the turn authority is overshooting at direction changes, so the next step is controller entry speed rather than more turn authority. If s-bend steering_oscillation rises above 0.35, return wheel_track to 0.10 m and keep the iteration 7 design.
requested_changes: Keep the iteration 7 design and set wheel_track to 0.09 m. Iteration 7 showed the slalom progress rising with lower yaw inertia (0.30 to 0.53), and iteration 4 vs 1 showed narrower track helps the slalom without hurting the oval (20/20 both ways).
If s-bend steering_oscillation rises above 0.35 or the oval loses any trials at 0.09 m, return wheel_track to 0.10 m, since iteration 7 measured s-bend 0.311 and oval 20/20 at 0.10 m.

If slalom line_loss_events stay at 1.3 or rise with max_error at or above 0.065, do not reduce wheel_track further; report the heading at first line loss so the next step can change the controller's entry speed rather than the geometry.
